title: Vertical product topology and its coefficient sheaf
statement: Let J and C be small categories, K a Grothendieck topology on C, and O a sheaf of commutative rings on C. There is a topology T on J^op × C in which a sieve S on (op j,U) covers exactly when its pullback along V ↦ (op j,V) covers U in K. In particular the coefficient presheaf R(j,U)=O(U), whose horizontal restrictions are identities, is a sheaf of rings. These objects are constructed explicitly, not selected from existence statements.

proof.text: Define covering sieves by their vertical slices. Maximality is inherited from K. The vertical slice of a pullback contains the pullback of the original slice, so upward closure and pullback stability in K prove stability. For transitivity restrict the local covering assumptions to the vertical arrows and apply transitivity in K.

proof.text: For set-valued presheaves, a matching family on a vertical cover extends to its product-sieve pullback using horizontal restrictions; gluing in the product implies gluing on the slice. Conversely glue the vertical part of a product matching family and check every other arrow by separatedness on the pullback of the vertical cover. Apply this criterion after every coyoneda functor to obtain the categorical sheaf criterion.

proof.text: Define R as the second-projection pullback of O. Its vertical restrictions are O, so the criterion proves the sheaf condition. The topology and presheaf equalities are definitional.
